title: LayerStoRm Configuration
description: Configuration schema for LayerStoRm MoE LLM inference engine

vram_gb.description: GPU VRAM in GiB (CUDA-reported, e.g. 31.25 for RTX 5090); null = auto-detect from hardware

pcie_width.description: PCIe lane width (null = auto-detect from sysfs)

numa_node.description: NUMA node affinity (null = auto-detect from sysfs)

pcie_bandwidth_loss_ratio.description: Effective PCIe bandwidth as fraction of theoretical (accounts for protocol overhead, contention)

compute_weight.description: Relative compute throughput weight for GPU load balancing. null = auto from GPU type lookup (rtx5090=1.0, rtx5080=0.5). Higher = more work assigned. User-settable for unlisted GPU types or custom tuning.

vram_budget_gb.description: Usable VRAM cap in GB (null = auto-detect)

roles.description: GPU roles: attention = MLA/DSA compute, resident = pinned layers (dense FFN, embedding, gating, output head), expert_streaming = expert cache and streaming execution

vram_allocation_gb.description: Per-role VRAM budget for varying roles (null = auto: use remaining after fixed allocations)

resident.description: VRAM budget for pinned resident layers in GB (null = auto from pinned layer config)

expert_streaming.description: VRAM budget for expert cache in GB (null = use remaining after fixed allocations)

stable_zone_fraction.description: Per-GPU override for stable zone fraction within expert cache (null = use memory.expert_cache.stable_zone_fraction)

safety_margin_gb.description: Per-GPU override of memory.vram_safety_margin_gb (null = use the global value). The margin is VRAM left UNALLOCATED on this GPU for CUDA context, host-pinned-arena page tables (~3 MiB per pinned GiB), and late driver allocations — shaving it below the global default trades runtime headroom for a larger expert window (e.g. a TP GPU hosting a quantized DSpark draft, TD-DSPARK-DRAFT-SHARD window probe). The engine-level elastic superchunk/MoE-BIG headroom derivations keep using the GLOBAL margin (conservative).

ref.description: Lightweight GPU reference (INV-4.18). Set at parse time from id/type/position. Passed through all internal APIs.

pcie_gen_max.description: Device PCIe capability (max_link_speed from sysfs); internal, not parsed from config

pcie_width_max.description: Device max lane width capability; internal, not parsed from config

pci_bus_id.description: PCI Bus ID (0000:01:00.0); internal, not parsed from config

cpu_expert_object.description: A CPU NUMA-node expert-FFN device (C-6, NumaCpuExpertDevice). Runs the routed MoE expert FFN on host cores pinned to one NUMA node, reading nvfp4-sm1xx weights from that node's PinnedExpertArena slabs. Not a CUDA device — it has no GPU ordinal; it is appended to the engine's ExpertDevice list after the GPUs.

numa_node.description: NUMA node this CPU expert device pins its work to and sources weights from. Reused as GpuRef::id (NOT a CUDA ordinal) for the device's cpu GpuRef.

max_threads.description: Max fork-join threads (physical cores) for the FFN. 0 = use all physical cores on the node (SMT siblings dropped).

enabled.description: Construct this CPU expert device. false = skip (slot ignored).

mscale_all_dim.description: YaRN mscale_all_dim parameter (drives the softmax-scale mscale^2 factor)

original_max_position_embeddings.description: Pre-extension context length; YaRN frequency correction applies beyond it

preset.description: Name of a config preset. Preset values are merged under user values (user wins). May not set model, quantization, or hardware.

architecture.description: Model architecture class. deepseek_v4: DeepSeek-V4 family (native MQA-over-latent, CSA/HCA hybrid attention, mHC residual streams — spec/DEEPSEEK4_PLAN.md)

use_mmap.description: Use memory-mapped I/O for weight loading. When false, weights are read into heap-allocated buffers via pread.

n_routed_experts.description: Total number of routed experts per MoE layer

n_group.description: Number of expert groups for grouped routing

topk_group.description: Number of groups selected per token in grouped routing

vocab_size.description: Vocabulary size = the embedding / output-head tensor ROW count (the logits width, padding included). OPTIONAL: 0 (default) = AUTODETECT from the weights at load (the adopted value is logged). When set explicitly it is CROSS-CHECKED against the weights-derived width at load and a mismatch FAILS LOUD with both numbers (weights are ground truth; config is explicit intent; disagreement is always a bug — a wrong value would silently mis-size logits readbacks, sampling, and guided-decode grammar masks). Both weights formats are covered (safetensors model.embed_tokens.weight / GGUF token_embd.weight, output-head fallback).
vocab_size.x-devDoc: Resolved by model::resolve_vocab_size (weight_loader.cpp) called from Engine::init_modules and Engine::run_prepack BEFORE LayerRegistry/VramAllocator consume the value. Engine value re-exported as EngineInfo.vocab_size.

max_position_embeddings.description: Maximum sequence length supported by the model

index_topk.description: DSA top-K token selection (0 = DSA disabled)

index_topk_freq.description: IndexShare period: 1 in N post-lead layers recompute the indexer (a 'full' layer); the rest reuse the preceding full layer's top-k (a 'shared' layer). 0 = every layer is full (no sharing).

index_skip_topk_offset.description: IndexShare leading-full count: the first N layers are always full. Full-layer set = { l : l < offset OR (l - offset + 1) % index_topk_freq == 0 }.

indexer_rope_interleave.description: Use interleaved RoPE in DSA indexer

first_k_dense_replace.description: Number of initial layers using dense FFN instead of MoE

routed_scaling_factor.description: Scaling factor for routed expert outputs

moe_layer_freq.description: Frequency of MoE layers (1 = every eligible layer)

norm_topk_prob.description: Normalize routing probabilities after top-K selection. (Source: DeepSeek V3 Technical Report) [topk_gating.cu]

gating_score_fn.description: Scoring function for expert gating. sqrtsoftplus = sqrt(log(1+exp(x))) (DeepSeek V4; GGUF expert_gating_func 4; kernel: deps/LayerStoRmExpertKernels ScoringFunc::kSqrtSoftplus). (Source: DeepSeek V3/V4 Technical Reports) [adaptive_gating.cu, topk_gating.cu]

head_dim.description: V4 attention head dimension (nope + rope; V4-Flash: 512 = 448 + 64). Single shared KV latent of this width serves as BOTH K and V (MQA-over-latent, num_key_value_heads = 1). 0 (default) = not a V4 model; REQUIRED > 0 for deepseek_v4. For deepseek_v4 the MLA dims (kv_lora_rank, qk_nope_head_dim, v_head_dim) are IGNORED — head_dim and qk_rope_head_dim are authoritative.

compress_ratios.description: V4 per-layer attention compression ratios: 0 = sliding-window-only, 4 = CSA (compressed sparse attention + Lightning Indexer), 128 = HCA (heavily compressed, dense). Values must be in {0, 4, 128}. Length must be >= num_hidden_layers; entries beyond num_hidden_layers must be 0 (the HF/GGUF array carries trailing zeros for the MTP layers — V4-Flash ships 46 = 43 + 3) and are ignored. Empty (default) = non-V4 model; REQUIRED non-empty for deepseek_v4.

compress_rope_theta.description: V4 RoPE base frequency for COMPRESSED-attention layers (compress_ratios[l] != 0; V4-Flash: 160000). Compressed layers apply this theta WITH the model's yarn rope_scaling; uncompressed layers (compress_ratios[l] == 0) use rope_theta with NO yarn (freq_scale 1, ext_factor 0) — ref/llama.cpp/src/models/deepseek4.cpp. 0 (default) = non-V4 model.

sliding_window.description: V4 sliding-window size in tokens for the raw-KV attention branch (V4-Flash: 128). All V4 layers keep a raw window of this many recent tokens alongside any compressed tier. 0 (default) = no sliding window (non-V4 models).

swiglu_limit.description: SwiGLU clamp bound for expert FFN activations (V4: 10.0 on routed AND shared experts; GGUF swiglu_clamp_exp/_shexp). Kernel clamps gate to [-limit, limit] before SiLU and caps SiLU output at limit (deps/LayerStoRmExpertKernels FusedSwigluParams.swiglu_limit). 0 (default) = no clamp (V3.2/GLM behavior, zero overhead).

num_hash_layers.description: V4 hash-routed MoE layer count: layers l < num_hash_layers select experts via the ffn_gate_tid2eid token-id lookup table [num_experts_per_tok x vocab] instead of score-based top-K, and carry no exp_probs_b bias (V4-Flash: 3). 0 (default) = no hash layers.

o_groups.description: V4 grouped output-projection group count (V4-Flash: 8). o_proj is a 2-stage grouped low-rank factorization: per-group down-projection (attn_output_a) to o_lora_rank, then one shared up-projection (attn_output_b) to hidden. Must divide num_attention_heads. 1 (default) = standard ungrouped o_proj.

o_lora_rank.description: V4 grouped output-projection per-group rank (V4-Flash: 1024). REQUIRED > 0 when o_groups > 1. 0 (default) = no low-rank o_proj.

hc_mult.description: mHC (manifold-constrained hyper-connections) residual stream count (V4: 4). The residual state is [tokens, hc_mult, hidden]; every attn/FFN sublayer is wrapped in hc_pre (collapse + mix coefficients) / hc_post (re-expand), with a final output_hc collapse before the LM head. 1 (default) = standard single residual stream (no mHC).

hc_sinkhorn_iters.description: mHC Sinkhorn-Knopp iterations projecting the comb mixing matrix onto the Birkhoff polytope (doubly stochastic); V4: 20. Ignored when hc_mult == 1.

hc_eps.description: mHC epsilon: added to the sigmoid pre-mix weights and to Sinkhorn row/column normalization denominators; V4: 1e-6. Ignored when hc_mult == 1.

vision.description: Vision encoder configuration (Kimi K2.5). Currently unimplemented

enabled.description: Enable vision encoder. Currently unimplemented. (Source: Kimi K2.5) [vision_encoder.h]

hidden_size.description: Vision encoder hidden dimension. Currently unimplemented. (Source: Kimi K2.5) [vision_encoder.h]

num_layers.description: Vision encoder transformer layers. Currently unimplemented. (Source: Kimi K2.5) [vision_encoder.h]

num_heads.description: Vision encoder attention heads. Currently unimplemented. (Source: Kimi K2.5) [vision_encoder.h]

patch_size.description: Vision patch size. Currently unimplemented. (Source: Kimi K2.5) [vision_encoder.h]

image_size.description: Input image resolution. Currently unimplemented. (Source: Kimi K2.5) [vision_encoder.h]

weights.description: Model weight quantization format. Supported: nvfp4, fp8 (e4m3/e5m2), and GGUF. GGUF is per-tensor mixed precision: 'gguf' = real GGUF model, each tensor's k-quant type comes from the file metadata (the normal case). 'gguf_q2_k'/'q3_k'/'q4_k'/'q5_k'/'q6_k'/'q8_0'/'mxfp4' = uniform override forcing one type for every tensor (synthetic/test weights; mxfp4 = OCP MX e2m1 + E8M0 block scale, 17 B / 32 values — DeepSeek-V4 QAT routed experts). int4_symmetric/int4_asymmetric are reserved.

gguf_strategy.description: GGUF weight-GEMM strategy: int = Q8_1 dp4a/int8 tensor-core (fast, ~8-bit activation error); dequant = dequant-to-float (lossless activation). Applies to all GGUF weight GEMMs. GGUF-only; ignored when 'weights' is not a gguf_* type.

attention_compute.description: Attention computation precision. Only fp8_e4m3 is currently supported

kv_cache.description: KV cache storage precision. Only fp8_e4m3 is currently supported

gating_compute.description: Router/gating computation precision. Only fp32 is currently supported

cpu_expert_devices.description: CPU NUMA-node expert-FFN devices (C-6). Each entry adds a NumaCpuExpertDevice for one NUMA node, appended to the ExpertDevice list after the GPUs. Empty = GPU-only experts (default).

tp_array.description: GPU IDs for TP group (null = auto-detect). Length must be power of 2.

system_ram_gb.description: Total system RAM in GB (null = auto-detect from /proc/meminfo)

nvme_paths.description: NVMe mount point(s) for cold tier. Multiple paths enable balanced multi-NVMe loading.
nvme_paths.x-devDoc: Empty array disables NVMe tier entirely. NvmeTier creates one io_uring ring per physical drive (INV-4.12c). Expert-to-drive assignment is deterministic (hash of ExpertKey). NvmeTier manages warm cache (host RAM) + cold storage (NVMe); ExpertCache manages hot tier (VRAM).

dcp_enabled.description: Data-Context Parallelism flag. Auto-set by resolver: true when tensor_parallelism >= 2. Not user-configurable.

dcp_indexer_mode.description: DSA indexer K cache strategy with DCP. 'replicated': full indexer K on each GPU for exact global top-k scoring. 'local': indexer K sharded round-robin by indexer page (owner = (pos / indexer_k_page_size_tokens) % tp); each GPU scores only its own shard and the per-rank top-k candidates are allgathered and exactly re-merged into the same global top-k (TD-GLM-INDEXER-LOCAL-MERGE) — halves resident indexer K per GPU (~390 MB at 100K context) at the cost of a tiny per-layer candidate allgather. Only affects DSA models (index_topk > 0). Ignored when tensor_parallelism < 2.

dcp_kv_mode.description: KV cache strategy with DCP (Helix sequence sharding, INV-DCP-6). 'sharded' (DEFAULT): KV is sequence-sharded by token position across ranks (INV-4.9e disjoint round-robin chunks) — each rank attends only its token shard and the DCP LSE combine merges the partial outputs (INV-DCP-KVREP: the combine runs ONLY in this mode). Halves per-GPU KV footprint and is the measured champion recipe (+4.6% end-to-end on the dsp52 champion, 2026-08-17 — replicated doubles KvTiering materialization). 'replicated' (opt-in): every TP rank stores the full KV cache and computes complete attention over its head shard (the legacy validated mode; the only mode where sparse chunk PREFILL is consumed sparse — TD-SPARSE-PREFILL-KVS; DSA sparse DECODE works in both modes). Ignored when tensor_parallelism < 2.
dcp_kv_mode.x-devDoc: Wired to DcpExecutor::Options::dcp_kv_sharded and CommandDispatcher::build_kv_metadata's sharded branch (KVS-2). Under 'sharded' the split is per shape: DSA sparse DECODE stays active — each rank consumes the KVS-4 translated LOCAL top-k selection (dispatch_attention.cpp TD-KVT-DCP-SHARDED seam, INV-KVT-9) — but sparse chunk PREFILL dense-fallbacks (prefill_sparse_tierable gate excludes kv_sharded_ && dcp_size >= 2; TD-SPARSE-PREFILL-KVS), and B>1 chunk cohorts are dense in every mode. HiSparse KV tiering remains fully active for decode under sharded (prefill chunks non-tierable there, lifted by full cold-page re-promotion).

attention.description: Attention layers to pin in VRAM

dense_ffn_layers.description: Dense FFN layer indices to pin

gating.description: Gating/router layers to pin in VRAM

default_mode.description: Default TP mode for components without an explicit field (null = inherit from parallelism.tensor_parallelism)

gating.description: TP mode for gating layers (null = inherit from parallelism.tensor_parallelism)

pinned_dense_ffn.description: TP mode for pinned dense FFN layers (null = inherit from parallelism.tensor_parallelism)

attention.description: TP mode for attention layers (null = inherit from parallelism.tensor_parallelism)

shared_expert.description: TP mode for shared expert layers (null = inherit from parallelism.tensor_parallelism)

embedding.description: TP mode for embedding layer (null = inherit from parallelism.tensor_parallelism)

output_head.description: TP mode for output head (lm_head) (null = inherit from parallelism.tensor_parallelism)

max_pages_per_gpu.description: KV cache PHYSICAL pages per GPU: one page per (sequence, logical page, layer) per INV-KV-LAYER, so an explicit value must include the ×num_layers (incl. MTP) factor; auto sizing does

speculation_pool_fraction.description: Fraction of KV pages reserved for speculation

indexer_k_page_size_tokens.description: Page size in tokens for DSA indexer K cache. Only used when model has DSA (index_topk > 0). Coarse default: at ~132 B/token the block-table overhead is negligible and a growing sequence claims ~1 MB chunks on demand (amortized-growth behavior with no copies); lower toward 64 only for many-sequence serving where fine-grained multiplexing matters.
indexer_k_page_size_tokens.x-devDoc: PageAllocator Pool::kIndexerK uses this as its page granularity. Separate pool with own base pointer, metadata array, and free list (INV-4.9d). Replication/sharding governed by hardware.dcp_indexer_mode. Page size is a pure capacity-multiplexing policy knob — same code path at any value (see TD-GLM-INDEXER-PAGED).

prefill_scratch_preallocated_gb.description: Pre-allocated scratch at tail of KV main pool for prefill workspace (GB). Forms contiguous buffer with streaming spill zone.

streaming_spill_fraction.description: Fraction of streaming zone used as spill zone (top, repurposable for prefill scratch). Remainder is pre-allocated expert prefetch (bottom, permanent).

dcp_chunk_size.description: Consecutive tokens per DCP rank before rotating to the next rank. Round-robin chunking per Helix S2.3. Only used when tensor_parallelism >= 2. Must be a multiple of page_size_tokens.

naive_prefill_context_ceiling.description: Maximum context length (tokens) for dense naive prefill. Beyond this ceiling, absorbed prefill is used directly (zero scratch, no expert eviction from spill zone). null = no ceiling (use naive whenever scratch fits). Set to limit decompression buffer size and support larger max_sequence_length via absorbed fallback.

page_growth_chunk_tokens.description: Tokens of headroom beyond prompt_len on CMD_SEQ_CREATE, and auto-growth chunk size in build_kv_metadata. 0 disables.

fragmentation_tolerance.description: Max internal fragmentation from block alignment before compaction. (Source: PagedAttention/vLLM) [kv_cache.h]

kv_tiering.description: GLM-25k: DSA-guided KV tiering (HiSparse-style). Demotes cold main-KV pages to NUMA-local pinned host RAM and materializes exactly the indexer's selected rows into a dense per-layer scratch before sparse attention. Placement-only: token-identical to the non-tiered path by construction (INV-KVT-1). Requires a DSA model (index_topk > 0), replicated KV, snapmla backend, B==1 decode.

enabled.description: Enable DSA-guided KV tiering. Off = non-tiered path byte-identical.

hot_buffer_slots.description: Per-layer hot row-cache capacity in token slots AND paged-pool retention window in tokens (HiSparse device_buffer_size analogue, ~2-3x index_topk). 0 = auto (2x index_topk).

host_to_device_ratio.description: Cold host-pool capacity as a multiple of the per-layer hot buffer (HiSparse host_to_device_ratio). When the pool is full further demotions are skipped (pages stay hot, fail-safe).

replica_cold_dedup.description: Under REPLICATED KV at dcp>=2, keep a single cold copy per demoted page (round-robin cold-owner rank) instead of one per rank: pinned cold host RAM divided by dcp, total capacity unchanged. Demotion D2H and cold-burst H2D DMAs stay NUMA-node-local; only the cold-fetch host memcpy may cross nodes for non-owner ranks (INV-KVT-11). Placement-only, token-identical. Ignored under sharded KV (already single-copy) and at dcp==1. Disable to restore per-rank cold copies (all-local host memcpy, dcp x host RAM).

eviction_gamma_routing_weight.description: Routing weight impact in eviction scoring

eviction_delta_temporal_autocorr.description: Temporal autocorrelation weight in eviction scoring

eviction_zeta_prefetch_score.description: Prefetch signal weight in eviction scoring

eviction_eta_hysteresis.description: Hysteresis state weight in eviction scoring. Higher = more protection for frequently-activated experts. Only effective when hysteresis_enabled is true. (Source: MoE-SpAc, arXiv 2603.09983)

hysteresis_enabled.description: Enable MoE-SpAc per-expert hysteresis state machine to prevent cache thrashing. When enabled, experts build up caching priority through repeated activation and only lose it gradually. (Source: MoE-SpAc, arXiv 2603.09983)

hysteresis_stages.description: Number of hysteresis state levels (TOP_STAT). Higher = more granular caching priority.

hysteresis_up_threshold.description: Activation count above current state required for promotion. Higher = harder to promote (more stable).

hysteresis_down_threshold.description: Activation count below current state required for demotion. Lower = easier to demote.

duplication_frequency_threshold_percenti.description: Percentile threshold for expert duplication candidates

temporal_autocorrelation_bonus.description: Bonus for temporal autocorrelation in eviction

stable_zone_fraction.description: Fraction of expert cache VRAM reserved for the stable zone (co-activation placements, high-frequency experts with slow eviction). The remaining fraction is the streaming zone (speculative prefetch, layer-ahead loads with fast turnover). Per-GPU override available in gpu_object.vram_allocation_gb.stable_zone_fraction
stable_zone_fraction.x-devDoc: TransferScheduler uses this value as zone routing threshold: PrefetchPriority >= stable_zone_fraction routes to kStable, below routes to kStreaming. Eviction policy scores both zones but streaming evicts first (kStreamingZoneBonus=500.0 additive). Two-phase protocol: reserve() then mark_ready() (INV-4.5.1).

inclusive_cache.description: Inclusive cache hierarchy (INV-4.12e). When true (default), each tier retains data after promotion — VRAM eviction is metadata-only. When false, host RAM copies are freed after H2D, requiring D_CMD_SLOW_EVICT_TO_HOST for safe VRAM eviction.

layer_depth_decay_factor.description: Exponential decay for eviction priority by layer depth; deeper layers = less priority. (Source: MoE Infinity) [expert_cache.h]

entropy_aware_eviction.description: Weight eviction by token entropy; high-entropy tokens = less predictable routing = higher eviction priority. (Source: MoE-SpeQ) [expert_cache.h]

prefetch_ahead_layers.description: Layers ahead to prefetch from NVMe

host_ram_cache_gb.description: Host RAM budget for warm expert cache in GB (null = auto: system_ram - pinned - OS reserve)
host_ram_cache_gb.x-devDoc: Inclusive cache hierarchy (INV-4.12e): host RAM retains copies after H2D promotion. Host RAM eviction is pure LRU (INV-4.12d), simpler than VRAM impact-weighted eviction. Host eviction skips NVMe write when NVMe copy already exists.

direct_io.description: Use O_DIRECT for NVMe I/O (bypasses page cache, reduces memory pressure)
direct_io.x-devDoc: When true, NVMe reads bypass kernel page cache via O_DIRECT flag on io_uring submissions. Reduces host memory pressure but requires page-aligned buffers (NvmeTier handles alignment internally).

vram_safety_margin_gb.description: Per-GPU VRAM reserved for CUDA context, driver, streams, and cuBLAS handles (GB)
vram_safety_margin_gb.x-devDoc: VramAllocator allocates (total_vram - safety_margin) as one contiguous block per GPU. Must cover CUDA context, cuBLAS handles, NCCL comm buffers, stream allocations, and driver overhead. Increase if cudaMalloc fails during init.

host_packed_cache_mb.description: Host RAM budget (MB) for retaining packed expert buffers across prefetch cycles. 0 = release after H2D (default, matches legacy TD-82a behavior). -1 = unlimited (never evicts). N > 0 = bounded LRU cache. Reduces ~1ms/expert NVFP4 re-packing cost on re-prefetch.
host_packed_cache_mb.x-devDoc: PackedBufferCache (WP-4). In explicit mode, malloc+LRU with this budget. In mmap mode (preprocessing.host_cache_mode=mmap with prepacked files), this field is ignored — OS page cache manages residency. Eviction uses shared_ptr::use_count() > 1 to skip entries with in-flight DMA references (safe under INV-ELM-1 single-threaded daemon).

preload_expert_buffers.description: Eagerly populate host packed buffer cache at startup. In explicit mode: pack all experts and insert (stops when budget is full). In mmap mode: madvise(MADV_WILLNEED) on prepacked file regions. Adds startup latency (~15s for V3.2) but eliminates runtime packing.
preload_expert_buffers.x-devDoc: PackedBufferCache (WP-4) preload. Explicit mode calls ensure_expert_packed() for all routed experts and inserts owned_buf into cache. Mmap mode calls madvise on PrepackedSource mmap regions. No-op if host_packed_cache_mb=0 in explicit mode.

pin_host_expert_pool.description: Page-lock the host expert pool, NUMA-bound to each expert's home node, so H2D DMAs the source directly at full PCIe bandwidth (no staging copy). Requires preload_expert_buffers. P-24: builds one anonymous mbind'd arena per GPU-attached NUMA node and registers it ONCE with cudaHostRegisterPortable (~tens of ms/GB), slab-managed with LRU + a multi-GPU in-flight refcount; expert preload becomes a plain file read into a pinned slot. Startup is seconds/node (vs the 481-1 per-file path's ~5.7 s/GB, TD-100c). Leave off for fast test/dev startup (falls back to the mmap + pinned staging pool — byte-for-byte today's behavior). 481-1/P-23/P-24.
pin_host_expert_pool.x-devDoc: When on, Engine builds a memory::PinnedExpertArena (one PinnedNodeArena per node) and wires it as host_source priority -1 (PinnedExpertArena* in HostSourceDeps); resolve fills a slot via PrepackedSource::load_into on miss and returns pinned=true. When off, host_source uses the mmap path (preload_mmap madvise) + staging pool. cudaHostRegisterReadOnly is unsupported on SM120; the arena is anonymous writable memory so Portable register succeeds fast.

pin_host_expert_pool_sizing.description: Per-NUMA-node budget for pin_host_expert_pool (replaces the legacy pin_host_expert_pool_fraction). A global mode/value plus optional per-node overrides; the arena slab is capped at this budget per node (and never exceeds the full routed-expert set). Regions over budget fall back to staging. Prevents oversubscribing a node (INV-4.12f).

mode.description: fraction_free: value x node available RAM (MemFree + reclaimable page cache + SReclaimable). fraction_total: value x node MemTotal. absolute_gb: value GB flat (decimals ok).

value.description: Fraction in (0,1] for fraction_* modes, or GB (>0, decimals ok) for absolute_gb. Default 0.9 = the keeper52 full-fit arena (paired with the pin_host_expert_pool_preload + direct O_DIRECT defaults, so the page cache is not relied on). With preload/direct OFF, prefer ~0.15: a larger lazy arena evicts the prepacked file's page cache (which backs cold loads), forcing them to disk and collapsing tok/s when the prepacked store is comparable to total RAM.

per_node.description: Per-NUMA-node overrides of {mode,value}, keyed by node index. A node absent here uses the global mode/value.

value.description: Fraction in (0,1] or GB (>0) per mode.

pin_host_expert_pool_extra_scratch_bytes.description: Bytes of GENERAL shared scratch reserved at the FRONT of EACH per-NUMA-node pinned arena (PinnedNodeArena), before the normal expert-slot region. The slot region starts after this reservation; expert slot pointers and capacity are unaffected by its presence other than the offset. Default 0 = byte-for-byte the prior arena layout (no scratch, zero behavior change). First consumer: MultiNumaCpuExpertDevice (C-6), which stages a node's contiguous N-row weight slices into this scratch so each node computes its expert-FFN partition from LOCAL, page-locked, NUMA-bound memory. The reservation is pinned + mbind'd to the node along with the rest of the arena slab.
pin_host_expert_pool_extra_scratch_bytes.x-devDoc: Threaded into memory::PinnedExpertArena(numa, slot_size, total, sizing, spill, extra_scratch_bytes) → each PinnedNodeArena allocates extra_scratch_bytes (page-rounded) at base_, exposes node_scratch()/node_scratch_bytes(), and offsets slot 0 to base_ + scratch. total_bytes_ = scratch + num_slots*slot_size.

pin_host_expert_pool_preload.description: Eagerly load the pinned arena from the prepacked source at startup (warm-by-definition) instead of lazily on first miss, then drop the prepacked mmap page cache (MADV_DONTNEED). Removes the runtime dependency on the prepacked page cache (which a large arena would otherwise evict, forcing cold loads to disk). Each node arena is loaded to capacity with its home-node experts; experts beyond capacity stay on the cold path. Adds startup latency (one bulk read of the pinned bytes). NOTE: this preloads expert WEIGHTS into host RAM — unrelated to LLM prefill (prompt/KV-cache processing). Requires pin_host_expert_pool.
pin_host_expert_pool_preload.x-devDoc: Engine calls PinnedExpertArena::preload(prepacked_source, num_hidden_layers, n_routed_experts) after building the arena + ArenaLoader, then PrepackedSource::advise_dontneed(). preload iterates expert-major, skips non-MoE layers via PrepackedSource::has(key), and reserve+load_into+mark_ready until each node arena is full.

cross_node_spill.description: Weighted cross-NUMA-node RAM spill tier for the pinned expert arena. When a computing GPU's local-node arena is full, an overflowing expert is placed in another node's RAM arena (including a GPU-less node) instead of being evicted to disk — the multi-node arenas act as one warm cache, NVMe is the last resort. A cross-NUMA H2D is slower (~-38%, INV-4.12h) but ~10x faster than an NVMe reload. Requires pin_host_expert_pool.

enabled.description: Enable the cross-node RAM spill tier (keeper52 default). NOTE: takes effect only with a non-empty `nodes` list (there is no auto node discovery; an empty list = no spill arenas — a config wanting the full-fit arena must list its spill nodes, see the GLM-5.2 configs). When false, the arena is GPU-attached-node-only — strict no-op.

nodes.description: Candidate spill nodes with weights. Higher weight is consistently preferred until that node fills, then the next; equal weights interleave (fewest-occupied). A node may be GPU-less (e.g. idle node 1) or a GPU node not currently computing (e.g. node 0). The computing GPU's own local node is always tier-1 and excluded from spill selection.

weight.description: Spill preference weight (>0 to be a candidate; higher fills first).

sizing_mode.description: How each spill node's arena is sized (independent of pin_host_expert_pool_sizing; no /total clamp — spill is extra capacity). A GPU-less spill node can be sized generously.

sizing_value.description: Fraction in (0,1] for fraction_* modes, or GB (>0) for absolute_gb, applied to each spill node (0.9 = keeper52 full-fit).

per_node.description: Per-NUMA-node overrides of {mode,value} for spill nodes (TD-NUMA-HBM-BANKS): e.g. size the small CPU-less HBM nodes by fraction_free (safe against the tiny node's free capacity) while big RAM spill nodes keep the global fraction_total. A node absent here uses sizing_mode/sizing_value.

value.description: Fraction in (0,1] or GB (>0) per mode.

pin_host_expert_pool_direct_load.description: Stage 2: read expert slots directly from the prepacked files (pread) instead of via mmap memcpy, so the page cache never competes with the pinned arena (the arena/spill RAM is the deterministic warm tier). In direct mode the prepacked files are NOT mmapped — fds are kept open and reads pread into the slot. null (default) = mirror pin_host_expert_pool_preload (on when preload is on). Requires pin_host_expert_pool. With cross_node_spill this is the regime where spill beats disk.
pin_host_expert_pool_direct_load.x-devDoc: Engine computes effective = direct_load.value_or(preload) and passes {direct, o_direct} to PrepackedSource. load_into() dispatches to pread_into() in direct mode; resolve()/host_ptr() return null (no mmap); host_source returns kPending when reserve_for_fill is momentarily full (no mmap fallback).

pin_host_expert_pool_direct_o_direct.description: When pin_host_expert_pool_direct_load is on: true → O_DIRECT reads (truly bypass the page cache; requires slot_size + offsets + slot buffers 4096-aligned, else falls back to buffered with a warning); false (default) → buffered pread + posix_fadvise(DONTNEED) on the just-read range (any slot size, no alignment constraint). NOTE: measured ~14% SLOWER than buffered (no readahead/caching) — leave off unless your hardware favors it.

pin_host_expert_pool_iouring.description: Stage 3: use an io_uring backend for the ArenaLoader cold reads — submit reads to a ring and reap completions on the daemon poll, with NO worker threads, so concurrency = queue depth (≫ a thread pool) and many misses in one fetch overlap. Requires pin_host_expert_pool_direct_load (needs open fds) and a liburing build (cmake -DLAYERSTORM_USE_NVME=ON); falls back to the worker pool otherwise. Forward-looking: helps the many-concurrent-misses regime; the current bottleneck is the fetch round-trip, not read concurrency.
pin_host_expert_pool_iouring.x-devDoc: Engine builds ArenaLoader with Backend::kIoUring when set AND PrepackedSource is in direct mode; submit() issues io_uring_prep_read on the prepacked fd into the pinned slot, poll_completed() reaps CQEs.

pin_host_expert_pool_thp.description: Transparent huge pages for the persistent-arena shared segments (madvise(MADV_HUGEPAGE) before first touch): 512x fewer PTEs to pin makes the warm-attach cudaHostRegister dramatically cheaper and relieves CPU-expert GEMV TLB pressure. Requires the kernel's shmem THP mode to allow madvise (/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/shmem_enabled = advise/always/within_size; NOT the default 'never' on many distros — e.g. `echo advise | sudo tee .../shmem_enabled`, not persisted across reboots). Falls back to 4K pages with a warning when disallowed. A store created with 4K pages stays 4K until its next cold rebuild. Only affects arena_attach shared segments.
pin_host_expert_pool_thp.x-devDoc: Engine calls NumaManager::set_shared_thp(cfg) before the arena build; NumaManager::advise_hugepage runs in allocate_on_node_shared (pre-fault — placement + hugeness both decided at first touch) and adopt_shared (future faults only). Detection: shmem_thp_available() parses the bracketed mode. Geometry identity (ArenaCache::hash_config) deliberately EXCLUDES page size.

arena_attach.description: P-24b persistent arena: back the pinned expert arena with memfd segments whose fds are kept alive by the CUDA-free `layerstorm_arena_holder` daemon, so the preloaded expert bytes (and their NUMA placement) survive engine restarts. On attach the engine validates the stored geometry/source identity (ArenaCache meta) and ADOPTS still-valid slots — skipping the NVMe preload for them; any mismatch (config geometry change, re-packed files via per-file mtime/size, schema bump) wipes and rebuilds cold — via a REASONED kWipe (kIdentityMismatch + the named failing check), which the holder honors while the holder PROCESS stays up to host the successor store, so a box can switch the model it serves without restarting the holder. Exactly ONE engine may be attached at a time (a second attach fails FATALLY — never silently double-allocates host RAM); detach is automatic on process exit/kill (the attachment IS the holder socket connection, INV-ARENA-HOLD). Requires pin_host_expert_pool + prepacked files.

enabled.description: Attach to (auto-spawning if needed) the arena holder. When the holder is unreachable the engine falls back to the classic process-private arena for that run (warning logged, no persistence). false = byte-for-byte the prior private-arena behavior.
enabled.x-devDoc: Engine builds memory::ArenaIpcClient + ArenaCache and passes ArenaBacking{kAdopt|kSharedCreate} to PinnedExpertArena. Warm validation: ArenaCache::hash_geometry over PinnedExpertArena::plan_geometry + hash_source_id(prepacked dir, manifest format_version, stride) vs the stored meta header; segment sizes byte-checked against slab_bytes(). Record stamping follows INV-ARENA-CACHE-ORDER (invalidate before first byte, ACTIVE only after load completes).

socket_path.description: Unix socket of the holder. A leading '@' selects the Linux abstract namespace (no filesystem entry — recommended). Use distinct paths to run independent persistent arenas (e.g. per model/box share).

holder_binary.description: Path to the layerstorm_arena_holder executable for auto_spawn. Empty = try build/tools/layerstorm_arena_holder (repo-root runs), then PATH.

auto_spawn.description: Spawn the holder (detached --daemon) when the socket is unreachable, then attach. false = attach only to an already-running holder (falls back to a private arena when absent).

persist.description: Store-protection mode for production serving: THIS engine never wipes or displaces the holder's store, and the store SURVIVES this engine's exit for the next boot to adopt. On warm-attach validation failure (identity/geometry mismatch) or any adoption error, the boot FAILS LOUD with the mismatch reason instead of silently wiping + cold-rebuilding — and there is no fallback to a process-private arena either (on a box sized around the store, a second full-size arena OOMs; 2026-08-18 incident: a mismatch wipe + rebuild destroyed a 504 GB warm store when the rebuilding engine was OOM-killed). Cold BUILD into an EMPTY holder is still allowed (persist protects an existing store, it does not prevent creating one). To intentionally rebuild: boot once with persist=false, or run `layerstorm_arena_ctl --wipe` with every engine stopped. false = historical behavior (mismatch wipes + rebuilds cold, adoption errors fall back to a private arena). ACKNOWLEDGED TRADE (2026-08-22, when the kWipe REASON contract landed): the holder now honors every reasoned wipe — kIdentityMismatch from a discovering engine, kOperatorRequest from the CLI — and its old --persist veto is RETIRED, so this config field is the ONLY thing protecting a precious store; any other engine reaching the same socket with persist=false (resolved on_conflict 'kill') WILL wipe it. Set persist=true on every production config that can reach the socket. Interacts with on_conflict: an absent on_conflict derives from persist (false → 'kill', true → 'fail'), and persist=true is compatible ONLY with on_conflict='fail' (rejected at config parse otherwise).
persist.x-devDoc: engine.cpp arena-early worker: the !ok mismatch branch and the catch-all both key on config::resolved_arena_on_conflict() — persist=true resolves to 'fail' → arena_early_.fatal (rethrown at join, engine-fatal) instead of wipe()/private-fallback. Holder-unreachable stays a private-arena fallback (no store exists to protect). Mismatch diagnostics name the failed check (meta-invalid | config-identity | node-count | slab-size) and that same string rides the kWipe as WipeRequest::detail on the 'kill' path.

on_conflict.description: What an attach-enabled engine does when the holder HAS a store but identity validation MISMATCHES (named checks: meta-invalid | config-identity | node-count | slab-size). 'kill': wipe the holder store and cold-rebuild it in place (the historical persist=false reaction, now explicit) — the wipe is REASONED (WipeReason::kIdentityMismatch carrying the named failing check, logged holder-side), the holder honors it and stays up to host the successor store. 'fail': fail the boot LOUDLY naming the failed check; the store stays untouched (the historical persist=true reaction, now selectable independently). 'new': LEAVE the holder store untouched and run THIS engine on a fresh process-private arena for the run — the same fallback machinery as when the holder is unreachable; persistence is bypassed for the run (loud warning) and the private arena is allocated BESIDE the retained store (fraction_free sizing shrinks it to the remaining RAM), so use only where host RAM allows. DEFAULT: 'kill' (the historical reaction). Under persist=true the only permitted and effective mode is 'fail', so an absent field there resolves to 'fail' — the behavior matrix for existing configs is unchanged. Compatibility, enforced at config PARSE (not at attach): persist=true is compatible ONLY with 'fail' — persist + 'kill' is a flat contradiction (persist means the store is never wiped), and persist + 'new' is contradictory too (the deployment declared its arena must be the persistent store; silently serving from a throwaway private arena would violate that and double-allocate ~500 GB host RAM behind the operator). A holder that does not speak the kWipe REASON contract (a binary older than 2026-08-22, or one started with the retired --persist flag) refuses the wipe (kError); the engine then ESCALATES to 'fail' naming the refusal — it never silently degrades to 'new'.
on_conflict.x-devDoc: engine.cpp arena_attach_early_worker_: the !ok mismatch branch switches on config::resolved_arena_on_conflict() (inline in config_validator.h; 'unset' resolves via persist). 'new' detaches (arena_ipc_.reset()) and returns → the late block builds the classic private arena, exactly the holder-unreachable path. 'kill' checks ArenaIpcClient::wipe()'s reply and escalates a holder refusal to arena_early_.fatal. The adoption-EXCEPTION catch-all keeps the historical matrix: 'fail' → fatal, 'kill'/'new' → private-arena fallback (no wipe — an adoption error is not an identity mismatch). Parse-time rejection: finalize_config (config_preset.cpp, throwing) + validate_arena_attach (config_validator.cpp, structured). x-unsetMember gives the C++ enum a JSON-invisible 'unset' first member so absence stays distinguishable from every explicit value.

arena_placement.description: M3 frequency-aware static arena placement (spec/reports/DSP52_BOOST.md M3, spec/reports/FETCH_XRAY.md): HBM-first + per-layer anti-gang slot→NUMA-node plan for the pinned expert arena, applied at arena BUILD (preload) time only. Performance-only: the same expert bytes DMA from a different host node — tokens are byte-identical ON vs OFF. The table's content hash folds into the ArenaCache store identity, so switching tables (or turning placement on/off) invalidates a persisted holder store and triggers ONE cold rebuild; subsequent warm attaches keep the placed layout.

freq_table.description: Path to the per-(layer,expert) fetch-count CSV ('layer,expert,count'; # comments allowed), e.g. tools/loader_xray/freq_table.py output over an LS_PERF_TRACE dump. "" = legacy frequency-blind placement. Relative paths resolve against the engine's working directory (same as the env var). Env LS_ARENA_PLACE_FREQ OVERRIDES this field: a path replaces it; 'off'/'none'/'0' force-disables (the way to get the legacy or pure-online placement when a model config carries a default table); unset/empty env defers here. Fail-closed: a configured-but-unreadable table aborts engine init.
freq_table.x-devDoc: memory::ArenaPlacementPolicy::resolve(cfg.memory.arena_placement.freq_table); identity = FNV-1a-64(tag + file bytes), path/source-agnostic. Interplay: arena_placement.online=true (the M3b migrator) treats a placed store as its bootstrap and refines it online; online=false keeps the static layout verbatim.

online.description: M3b online self-tuning arena placement (the EMA-driven migrator): observes live fetch traffic and migrates hot experts toward better NUMA nodes in the background, refining whatever layout the store booted with (static table or legacy). Byte-identical tokens ON vs OFF (placement is performance-only); migrations mutate the persisted holder store IN PLACE (no identity change, no rebuild). Default ON (2026-08-18 champion decision: online 10.459 tok/s vs 10.23-10.42 static anchors on dsp52; keeper prefers online per the M6 scoreboard; near-converged stores see ~10 migrations/run). No-ops with a warning when the pinned arena path or HBM arena nodes are absent. Env LS_ARENA_PLACE_ONLINE OVERRIDES this field: non-'0' forces ON, '0' forces OFF, unset defers here.
online.x-devDoc: Consumed in engine.cpp M3b migrator boot (env-over-config precedence there); arena_migrator.h documents the migrator knobs (still env-only tuning). The migrator requires the pinned arena + HBM nodes; absent => warn + disable, never fatal.

max_batch_size.description: Maximum tokens per batch in expert FFN

min_batch_tokens_per_expert.description: Minimum tokens to start expert batch

workload_shift_decay.description: Aggressive decay factor on workload shift detection

ewma_alpha.description: EWMA decay rate for workload detection

shift_threshold_std_devs.description: Standard deviations for shift detection threshold

token_window_size.description: Sliding window of tokens for workload distribution sampling. (Source: DALI) [workload_detector.h]

writer_yield_interval.description: Writer yields every N completed outermost transactions

publish_interval_us.description: Minimum interval between StateSnapshot publishes (us, measured from publish END). The spinning daemon otherwise publishes every ~us cycle, keeping the seqlock churning and starving Python readers (INV-IPC-PUBLISH-THROTTLE). 0 = publish every cycle (legacy; C++-only readers)

reader_max_retries.description: Max retry iterations before TimeoutError (~3min practical at ~850ns/iter, ~2min theoretical at ~547ns/iter sched_yield)

reader_stage0_yield_every.description: In stage 0 (tight spin), yield every N iterations

top_k.description: Max experts per token to consider from gating output

score_threshold.description: Min routing weight to include expert in prefetch hints

predictor_enabled.description: Enable LLaPor learned predictor (MEDIUM confidence, zero GPU cost). Predictor params in _internal-prescope section.

probe_points.description: Network depth fractions for probe insertion points

confidence_threshold.description: Minimum prediction confidence to trigger prefetch

training_buffer_size.description: Ring buffer size for training samples

speculative.description: Speculative prefetch from draft gating outputs. (Source: SP-MoE) [speculative_prefetch.h]

enabled.description: Enable speculative prefetch from draft gating outputs. (Source: SP-MoE) [speculative_prefetch.h]

max_prefetch_depth_layers.description: Max layers ahead to prefetch from draft gating; cache thrashing starts beyond 3. (Source: SP-MoE) [speculative_prefetch.h]

confidence_threshold.description: Min draft gating confidence to trigger prefetch. (Source: SP-MoE) [speculative_prefetch.h]

sp_moe_delta.description: SP-MoE speculative signal weight in prefetch fusion scoring. (Source: SP-MoE) [prefetch_fuser.h]

method.description: Engine-side (C++) speculative-decoding method, constructed via make_speculation_method at engine init (src/speculation/). none (DEFAULT): no method constructed — byte-identical to non-speculative behavior. null: no-op stub (drafts nothing; plumbing/diagnostic only). mtp: MtpSpeculationMethod (#16 / GLM-25g) — self-draft off the frozen trunk via the model's MTP head (requires num_nextn_predict_layers >= 1 and speculation.mtp.enabled). prompt_lookup: reserved — engine init fails until the concrete method lands. dspark: reserved (DSP-1 config surface; the DSparkSpeculationMethod lands in DSP-5) — engine init fails closed. Init-time selection (not hot-reloadable). Orthogonal to the sibling speculation.* sub-sections (mtp/dspark/prompt_lookup/... tuning knobs consumed by the selected method and the Phase-12 orchestrator pipelines).

confidence_threshold.description: Dynamic-depth early exit: stop chaining MTP draft steps when the previous step's top-1 probability falls below this threshold (dynamic_depth only; step 0 always runs). Mirrors orchestrator MtpDraftConfig.confidence_threshold.

batched_verify.description: Verify the round's K MTP draft tokens in ONE teacher-forced K+1-token forward on the MAIN sequence (chunked-prefill-shaped attention + FETCH_AND_RUN_MOE over the batch + multi-token OUTPUT_HEAD argmax readback) instead of K+1 sequential full-model feeds - the throughput-bearing mode. Lossless either way (INV-MTP-LOSSLESS: only main-model outputs are ever committed). false = the sequential early-stop schedule (the MtpLossless golden's reference shape). Mirrors orchestrator MtpDraftConfig.batched_verify.

dspark.description: DSpark — confidence-scheduled speculative decoding (Phase 28; spec/DSpark_NOTES.md). Semi-autoregressive draft: parallel DFlash-style backbone emits base logits/hiddens for a whole block in ONE forward, then a lightweight sequential Markov head adds intra-block dependency left-to-right; a trained confidence head + hardware-aware prefix scheduler pick per-request verification lengths. Knobs consumed by the dspark SpeculationMethod (DSP-5) and the DSP-6..DSP-9 confidence/scheduler pipeline. (Source: DSpark, DeepSeek-AI + PKU 2026; reference engines vLLM @8484ca5d, DeepSpec @afdfa7c)

block_size.description: Draft block size γ: tokens drafted per DSpark step (γ inputs → γ logits, anchor-as-first-prediction — INV-DSPARK-ANCHOR). One backbone forward covers the whole block, so draft latency is ~independent of γ. Default 8 = the shipped RedHatAI GLM-5.2 speculator checkpoint (speculators v0.5, block_size 8 / speculative_tokens 7); must match the trained checkpoint (DSP-2 cross-validates). The paper sweeps up to 16 offline.

speculative_tokens.description: Tokens proposed per block (speculators_config.proposal_methods[0].speculative_tokens). γ−1 in the shipped checkpoint (block 8 → anchor + 7 speculative). Must match the trained checkpoint; must not exceed block_size.

aux_hidden_state_layer_ids.description: TARGET layer indices whose hidden states feed the draft's EAGLE-style fc fusion (fc.weight [hidden, N_aux*hidden] over their concat). Strictly increasing; each < model.num_hidden_layers. Default = the shipped GLM-5.2 speculator ([8,23,39,55,70] of 78 target layers). Must match the trained checkpoint; DSP-3 exports these hiddens from the target forward.

mask_token_id.description: Token id whose embedding row serves as the DFlash mask/query-slot embedding (speculators v0.5 ships NO separate mask_embedding tensor — the row lives in the draft's embed_tokens). Indexes the draft's EMBED vocab (= the checkpoint transformer vocab_size, which can exceed a reduced draft_vocab_size); must be < max(draft_vocab_size, model.vocab_size) and match the trained checkpoint.

max_anchors.description: Maximum anchor positions per DSpark drafting pass (checkpoint max_anchors). Must match the trained checkpoint.

draft_vocab_size.description: Draft vocabulary size (lm_head/markov_w2 leading dim — the space the draft's logits and transition bias live in). Equals the GLM-5.2 target vocab (154880) in the shipped checkpoint (identity remap). Reduced-vocab checkpoints (draft_vocab_size < vocab_size) must ship a d2t [draft_vocab_size] I64 offset tensor; sampled draft ids are remapped on-device to target ids (target_id = draft_id + d2t[draft_id], vLLM convention). embed_tokens/markov_w1 stay target-vocab sized. Must match the trained checkpoint.

checkpoint_path.description: DSpark draft checkpoint: a DIRECTORY (speculators v0.5 format: config.json + model.safetensors — the GLM-5.2 speculator) or a `.gguf` FILE (ticket J: a `dflash`-arch DSpark speculator GGUF — the DeepSeek-V4-Flash draft; V4-shaped SWA-only blocks + MXFP4 MoE, single-rank only, embed/lm_head aliased from model.weights_path). Relative paths resolve against the engine working directory. Default = the RedHatAI GLM-5.2 speculator symlink used by the goldens.

draft_gpus.description: GPU positions (index into hardware.gpus[], INV-4.18) hosting the draft weights. Empty (DEFAULT) = auto: the first non-TP GPU (the secondary GPUs are idle while the TP GPUs run the target; the 7.61 GB BF16 GLM-5.2 draft fits a 16 GB 5080). DSP-2 places the WHOLE draft replicated on the first resolved GPU; TP-sharding across draft GPUs is deferred (TD-DSPARK-DRAFT-SHARD). Fails closed when empty and all GPUs are in hardware.tp_array.

draft_weights_quant.description: Requantize the DSpark draft's GEMM weight operands at upload (TD-DSPARK-DRAFT-QUANT): the 7 per-layer projections (q/k/v/o/gate/up/down) plus fc and lm_head are converted BF16 -> fp8_e4m3 (per-128-column-group FP32 scales, ~2x smaller) or nvfp4 (E2M1 g=16 + UE8M0 scales, ~3.5x smaller) and consumed by a fused-dequant GEMM; norms, embeddings, markov and confidence heads stay BF16. bf16 (DEFAULT) uploads verbatim — byte-identical to the pre-quant engine. Quantization is a drafting-QUALITY trade only (acceptance rate may dip; verification keeps the output lossless); it shrinks the draft's VRAM charge so the draft can host on a TP 5090 beside the target weights.
draft_weights_quant.x-affects: VRAM budget on the draft GPU (LayerRegistry dspark charge)

markov_rank.description: Rank r of the low-rank first-order Markov transition factorization B = W1·W2 (markov_w1 [V_draft, r] embedding lookup, markov_w2 [r, V_draft] logit projection). Must match the trained DeepSpec checkpoint.

head_type.description: Sequential head variant (DeepSpec markov_head.py: VanillaMarkov / GatedMarkovHead / RNNHead). markov is the deployed default (the only variant vLLM ships); gated and rnn are RESERVED enum values — selecting them fails closed until implemented.

confidence_enabled.description: Wire the trained per-position survival confidence head into inference (DSP-6). This is the TRAINED sigmoid survival estimator (cumprod-composable), NOT the output-head {top1_prob, entropy} heuristic (INV-DSPARK-CONF). Required for any scheduler_mode other than off.

scheduler_mode.description: Verification-length scheduling (DSP-9). off: fixed-block verification (vLLM-equivalent). static_threshold: per-request cutoff on cumulative survival a_{r,j} at confidence_threshold (DeepSpec-offline-eval-equivalent baseline). throughput: hardware-aware prefix scheduler, paper Alg. 1 — maximize Θ = τ·SPS(B) via the DSP-8 cost table. Non-off modes require confidence_enabled.

confidence_threshold.description: static_threshold scheduler mode: verify a draft position only while its (STS-calibrated) cumulative survival probability a_{r,j} stays >= this cutoff. Ignored by the other scheduler modes.

sts_temperatures.description: Sequential Temperature Scaling calibration temperatures, one per block position (length must equal block_size when non-empty). Empty (DEFAULT) = identity (no calibration). Fitted offline / filled by DSP-7 calibration.

draft_context_capacity_tokens.description: Capacity (tokens) of the draft backbone's context KV arena on the draft GPU (DSP-3): per layer, K and V rows of n_kv_heads*head_dim BF16 per target position, keyed by absolute position from the target's fused aux hiddens. Sequences longer than this fail closed for drafting (TD-DSPARK-CTX-CAP) — the target is unaffected. Default 8192 = max_anchors(1024) x block_size(8); 1.34 GB for the GLM-5.2 draft (5 layers x 4096 dims x 2 tensors x BF16).

aux_capture_max_rows.description: Row capacity of the aux-hidden capture staging buffer on the draft GPU (DSP-3): [rows, N_aux*hidden] BF16 receiving the target's exported layer hiddens before the fc fusion + context-KV ingest. Target steps larger than this (whole-prompt prefills, oversized prefill chunks) are ingested in staging-sized pieces per aux slot (chunked fc accumulation) — drafting stays armed up to draft_context_capacity_tokens, so this knob only sizes the staging/ingest granularity. Default 2048 rows = 126 MB for GLM-5.2 (5 x 6144 BF16 columns).

epm_dump_dir.description: EPM-1 training-data dump directory (spec/MoE-SpeQ_NOTES.md §7). Empty (DEFAULT) = OFF: zero overhead — no allocations, no extra copies or kernel work on any path. Non-empty = per-speculative-block raw dumps into this directory: the daemon appends EPMB records (draft per-backbone-layer residual hiddens [gamma, n_layers, hidden] BF16 + draft ids + raw c_k) to epm_blocks.bin after every D_CMD_RUN_DSPARK_STEP, and EPMR records (per decode position: all routed layers' 256 pre-top-k router logits FP16 + top-8 ids/weights from the F-1 attention-end gate — the exact buffers the FETCH_AND_RUN seam consumes) to epm_routing.bin; the Python orchestrator appends block metadata (anchor pos, draft/verify tokens, accepted length, c_k) to manifest.jsonl, joined on (seq_id, anchor_pos) by tools/elb_train/dataset.py. Dump-ON adds D2H+sync at every capture (timing changes are expected and irrelevant for collection). Env override: LS_EPM_DUMP=<dir> forces ON at <dir>; LS_EPM_DUMP=0 forces OFF.

verify_chunk_prefetch.description: Lever-4 verify-chunk expert prefetch (DSP52_BOOST campaign; batched verify only). During each batched verify chunk, at the LAUNCH of MoE layer L's attention (the H2D-idle window), the orchestrator fires ONE fire-and-forget D_B_CMD_PREFETCH_BATCH carrying the PREVIOUS chunk's layer-L routed expert union at its previous (expert, gpu) placement, at DMA priority -1.0 (strictly below demand fetches, which the FED issues at 0.0/kDemandFetchPriority). Advisory residency warm-up ONLY: the same weights land in the same cache seam the demand fetch would use, so tokens stay byte-identical prefetch-on vs prefetch-off (no numerics change, no routing change). Policy lives in the orchestrator (Python bridge / dsp52 test); the engine only executes the generic prefetch command. DEFAULT false: measured a NET LOSS on this DMA-bound box — -1.0% champion wall (9.562 vs 9.650 tok/s, 2026-08-17 arm C4), hit-neutral ~+0.6% wall tax under EPM-0, and the perfect-predictor oracle upper bound lost in every arm (top-1 -5.9%, all-misses -3.1%, bulk -7.5%). Kept as a reusable knob for future work (B>1 batching, sub-expert grain) where an idle H2D window may exist. prefill_superchunk_tokens.description: TD-PREFILL-SUPERCHUNK: decoupled prefill superchunk capacity in TOKENS. When > 0, the MoE pipeline scratch and the paired hidden-state buffers are sized for max(512, this many) tokens, so ONE FETCH_AND_RUN_MOE[_BIG] (or dense RUN_MOE) can batch the post-attention hidden states of K attention sub-chunks per layer — amortizing the per-layer routed-expert H2D fetch over K x chunk tokens while attention/tiering stay at the natural sub-chunk granularity (RUN_ATTENTION row_offset + superchunk flag). With prefill_moe_big (default on) this is the REQUEST; the effective capacity K is DERIVED at engine init from free VRAM (elastic, never OOM; 0 = derive up to the elastic bound) and reported in EngineInfo.moe_batch_capacity. With prefill_moe_big=false, 0 = disabled (byte-identical legacy sizing) and the legacy halving fail-safe applies.

prefill_moe_big.description: TD-PREFILL-MOE-BIG: never-OOM big-batch MoE (E_CMD_FETCH_AND_RUN_MOE_BIG + chunked grouped-GEMM execution). When true, the MoE TRANSIENT scratch (permute/gate-up/activation/expert-out/wave-accum/quant) is bounded at moe_big_chunk_tokens (~48 MB) instead of the full superchunk (~1.5 GB @2048 tok); any MoE dispatch whose token batch exceeds the chunk capacity runs the grouped GEMMs in chunks, reusing that scratch (only the [B,H] hidden output persists), and the effective superchunk capacity is DERIVED at engine init from free VRAM (elastic K — never OOM by construction; floor 512, cap 32768). Batches at or below the chunk capacity (all decode paths) run the byte-identical legacy single-shot pipeline. false = legacy sizing + single-shot only.

moe_big_chunk_tokens.description: TD-PREFILL-MOE-BIG: token chunk size for the chunked grouped-GEMM execution (prefill_moe_big). The MoE transient scratch is sized for this many tokens (x topk expansion) and reused across chunks; batches larger than max(this, orchestrator.max_batch_size) are processed chunk-by-chunk. LARGER IS FASTER until the transient set outgrows the ~512 MB prefill-scratch tail it is homed in: each grouped-GEMM sweep pays a ~(num_experts x tile_m=64) tile-row floor regardless of real rows (a 64-token chunk = avg 2 rows/expert against a 64-row tile), so total MoE cost scales with waves x ceil(batch/chunk) sweeps (measured 64-tok chunks ~4x slower than single-shot at n=876; see TD-MOE-BIG-GEMM-SWEEP). 512 tokens ~= 262 MB transients — still tail-resident.

dsa_sparse_prefill.description: DSA sparse CHUNK PREFILL attention (TD-SPARSE-CHUNK-PREFILL). When true, a dispatcher-blessed prefill/chunked-prefill step of a DSA model (index_topk > 0) runs the lightning indexer per chunk-query position and each chunk row attends only its own causal top-k (<= index_topk) selection instead of the DENSE full causal prefix — the pattern the model is TRAINED with (DeepSeek-V3.2/GLM-5.2 DSA is sparse end-to-end), removing the full-KV-attend prefill peak and enabling prefill KV tiering (TD-KVT-PREFILL half 2). Changes prefill numerics versus dense chunks (sparse selection prunes beyond index_topk context); validated against the DSA reference next-token. Default false: chunks stay dense (byte-identical legacy behavior). Requires replicated indexer + replicated KV in this pass — dcp_indexer_mode=local (TD-SPARSE-PREFILL-LOCAL-INDEXER) and dcp_kv_mode=sharded (TD-SPARSE-PREFILL-KVS) fall back to dense chunks.

dsa_indexer_rewind.description: INV-DSA-REWIND: bless SAME-SEQUENCE contiguous OVERWRITE-REWINDS in the DSA indexer coverage guard (pos0 <= high-water — the speculative batched-verify partial-acceptance re-feed shape) so those decode rows stay SPARSE-eligible instead of failing closed to per-row DENSE attention. Sound because every indexer-K append is POSITION-keyed: a re-feed overwrites its rows in place exactly as it overwrites the KV rows, and sparse validity comes from each step's own kv-meta seqlens bound. Token-correct either way; dense-vs-sparse kernel numerics differ in principle, but the dsp52 champion A/B (2026-08-18) measured IDENTICAL fingerprints (acc/tau/lookups) and a bit-identical 107-token trajectory on vs off — hence DEFAULT TRUE (production posture; sparse stays alive across speculative re-feeds). Gaps, mixed-sequence chunks, foreign sequences, and superchunk shapes stay fail-closed regardless. Env LS_INDEXER_REWIND OVERRIDES either way (set & !='0' -> on, '0' -> off, unset defers here). Set false for the legacy fail-closed guard (per-row dense fallback at pos < high-water).

deterministic_reduce.description: Bit-reproducible attention softmax-denominator reduction (DET-REDUCE Phase 1). When true (DEFAULT), the cross-warp denominator combine uses a fixed-order (vLLM block_sum-style) sum instead of warp-scheduling-order atomicAdd, eliminating run-to-run routing drift from near-tie flips. Perf-neutral (measured: full-pool keeper within noise; attention per-op marginally faster). Set false (or env LAYERSTORM_DETERMINISTIC_REDUCE=0) for the legacy atomic path.

deterministic_ep_combine.description: Placement-invariant MoE EP combine (DET-REDUCE Phase 1b). When true, the per-token routed expert sum is computed in a canonical fixed-slot order that is bit-identical regardless of which GPU holds each expert: each GPU writes its K per-slot contributions separately, the cross-GPU EP allreduce GATHERS slots, and a fixed-order K-reduce rounds to bf16 once — killing the placement->bf16->routing drift behind the spurious ACT+decay 'win'. Has a real cost (the routed EP-combine gather grows from [B,H] to [B,topk,H]), so DEFAULT false (opt-in). Payload precision is set by deterministic_ep_combine_precision. Override either way with env LAYERSTORM_DETERMINISTIC_EP_COMBINE (set & !=0 -> on, 0 -> off). Default-off is byte-identical to the legacy bf16 combine (goldens unchanged).

deterministic_ep_combine_precision.description: Per-slot payload precision for the placement-invariant MoE EP combine (only used when deterministic_ep_combine=true). bf16 (DEFAULT): per-slot contributions rounded to bf16 once and gathered as BF16 [B,topk,H] — HALF the gather bytes, with the K slots still accumulated in FP32 in fixed order (matches the vLLM/llama.cpp convention: fp32 math, 16-bit payload); collective −31% (decode) / −42% (B=8) vs fp32, measured. fp32: per-slot contributions gathered as FP32 [B,topk,H]. Placement-invariance holds for both (it comes from the fixed slot ORDER, not the payload dtype). Override with env LAYERSTORM_DETERMINISTIC_EP_COMBINE_PRECISION (bf16|fp32).

ipc_pin.description: TD-14d: CUDA-pin (cudaHostRegister, portable) the daemon's IPC shared region at engine init so every sideband D2H readback (CMD_SAMPLE_TOKENS token ids, D_CMD_RUN_DSPARK_STEP draft state, checkpoint payloads) is a TRUE async DMA. Unpinned, cudaMemcpyAsync into pageable host memory is internally synchronous and blocks the DAEMON THREAD until the SOURCE stream drains — measured 85.0 ms per DSpark draft readback (the whole draft pipeline queued ahead of it), serializing all command dispatch and defeating draft/target command-level overlap; pinned, the same handler costs 0.17 ms (DSP52_BOOST lever 2). DEFAULT true (production posture). The region is a private ~4.9 MB aligned_alloc mapping, disjoint from the pinned expert arena and every NUMA DMA buffer, so it can never partial-overlap another registration; registration failure is non-fatal (loud warn, sideband degrades to the pageable/blocking path) and the region is unregistered before its free at shutdown. Skipped entirely for null/CPU-only backends (skip_hardware_detection). Override either way with env LS_IPC_PIN (set & !=0 -> on, 0 -> off, unset defers here). Set false for the legacy unpinned sideband.

"" = legacy model_type-based parser. Consumed by the Python serving layer (server.tool_parsers registry); CLI override: --tool-call-parser.

enable_auto_tool_choice.description: Enable auto tool choice: run the named tool-call parser when a request carries tools and tool_choice is absent/"auto" (tool_choice "none" bypasses). Requires tool_call_parser. CLI override: --enable-auto-tool-choice.

reasoning_parser.description: Named reasoning parser (e.g. "glm45" for <think>...</think>, "deepseek_v4" for the structural start boundary): splits reasoning_content from content in chat responses, token-id based via the tokenizer's think-marker ids. "" = no reasoning split. Consumed by the Python serving layer (server.reasoning_parsers registry); CLI override: --reasoning-parser.

reasoning_config.description: JSON reasoning config passthrough (vLLM ReasoningConfig field names: reasoning_start_str/reasoning_end_str) — marker-string overrides for the named reasoning parser; empty markers = structural boundary (output begins in reasoning). "" = no overrides. Consumed by the Python serving layer; CLI override: --reasoning-config.

tokenizer_mode.description: Serving tokenizer mode (vLLM TokenizerMode parity subset). "auto" resolves from model.architecture (deepseek_v4 models -> "deepseek_v4", else "hf"); "deepseek_v4" switches chat-template kwarg normalization + thinking defaults to the DeepSeek-V4 rules (thinking defaults OFF; reasoning_effort none->off, max/xhigh->"max", other->"high"). Consumed by the Python serving layer; CLI override: --tokenizer-mode.

prefix_cache.description: Basic prompt-prefix KV caching (successor orchestrator, B=1): after each request's prompt prefill the orchestrator SEQ_FORKs a frozen PREFIX HOLDER sequence whose refcounted CoW pages keep the prompt's KV (VRAM + tiered host) resident; a later request whose prompt starts with a registered prefix forks FROM the holder and prefills only the delta. Token-identical ON vs OFF under the deterministic stack (INV-PREFIX-CACHE-1): reused KV bytes are the recomputed bytes; only prefill wall changes. Registry is LRU-bounded and evicts (frees holder sequences) on budget pressure or page-pool exhaustion.

enabled.description: Enable the prefix registry + SEQ_FORK reuse. false = byte-identical to the pre-cache request flow (create/prefill/free every request).

max_cached_tokens.description: LRU token budget: the sum of registered prefix lengths is kept at or below this by evicting oldest entries (0 = unbounded is NOT allowed; use enabled=false to disable). Retained holders are cheap in pages (shared refcounts + one CoW append-frontier logical page group per fork) but each pins its prefix's pages against reuse-by-free.

max_entries.description: Maximum retained prefix holder sequences (LRU). Also bounded by the engine page budget's max_concurrent_forks sizing.

prepacked_dir.description: Path to pre-processed expert directory (manifest.json + expert_NNN.bin). Empty = not available.

auto_preprocess.description: When true and no valid prepacked_dir, pre-process raw safetensors at engine init.

auto_preprocess_target.description: Directory to write auto-preprocessed files. Required when auto_preprocess=true and target is disk.

host_cache_mode.description: Host RAM caching strategy. 'mmap' = OS page cache. 'explicit_alloc' = engine-managed malloc+LRU.

legacy_weights.description: Force legacy weight loading (routed experts from safetensors) even when prepacked_dir exists. For A/B testing and migration validation.

gpu_loader.description: GPU loader transfer-cost calibration (spec/GPU_LOADER_MODEL.md, ticket I8b)

enabled.description: Run/load the GPU-loader calibration at init (off until the loader solver consumes the constants).

calibration_mode.description: loaded = load from calibration_path, falling back to a full calibration (and writing the file) if it is absent; quick = fast cache-hot benchmark; full = DDR-accurate (~32 GiB rotating footprint).

calibration_path.description: JSON file the loader constants are loaded from / written to. The calibration is weight/config-specific (the compute curve depends on the model's expert FFN dims), so it lives ADJACENT to the weights: an empty value (default) resolves to '<weights_path dir>/gpu_loader_calibration.json'; a bare filename resolves in the weights dir; an absolute path is used verbatim.
